text: Hey, it’s Marcus. Chapter 4 ended with Harriet badly hurt, struck by an iron weight that was meant for a runaway. Chapter 5 is called Not Worth a Sixpence. When I first read that title, it made me angry, because somebody says those words about Harriet. Today’s question: what do they miss about her? And who is she becoming while nobody is paying attention?

Freedom Watch: the strength nobody planned for. Master and the men who come to look at Harriet only see her worth in dollars. But during the long months in the cabin, something changes inside her that nobody can measure. In my research, this is the part I keep coming back to. Watch for the moment Sterling tells you how Harriet sees herself now.

Chapter 5 covers a lot of time, so watch the time words: holidays, seasons, even a year. Track how Harriet’s strength comes back, one step at a time. Notice where she keeps her money, and count it as it grows. Later you’ll meet someone new on the courthouse steps in Cambridge. I’ve walked those Cambridge streets. Read that part closely.

Hey, it’s Marcus. Chapter 5 ended with Master’s death, and with Harriet saying it out loud to John, one slow word at a time: I’m going to run away. He told her she’d never make it. In my research notes, Chapter 6 gets a whole page of its own. Today’s question: what does it take to step off the plantation, alone, toward a North you’ve never seen?

Freedom Watch: the moment of decision. On my tours, people asked me when Harriet made up her mind. I used to say it was one big moment. Now that I’ve read more, I’m not so sure. In this chapter, watch for every time she has a reason to stop, and what she does instead. The road she knows isn’t safe. The road north is a mystery. Which is scarier?

Before you open Chapter 6, get your sequence notes ready. This chapter moves fast, and the order matters. Watch the Quaker lady, and how carefully Harriet speaks to her. Listen for the words thee and thy; that’s how Quakers talked. Keep an eye on what Harriet carries, and on one thing she gives away. Listen for a song, too. Sterling prints every word of it.

Hey, it’s Marcus. At the end of Chapter 6, Harriet left her quilt on the Quaker lady’s doorstep and walked away singing. Now she’s on her own. In Chapter 7, the North Star is her guide. But a star only shines at night. Today’s question: when daylight comes and the star is gone, how does Harriet still find her way north?

Freedom Watch: the help of strangers. Harriet walks this whole chapter by herself, but she isn’t really alone. Some of her helpers aren’t even there. They gave her directions, or taught her something years ago. Others she meets for the very first time. In my research, I keep finding the same thing: almost every escape had helpers along the way. Count every one you find.

Chapter 7 is one long journey, so keep a clock in your head. The moon, the sun, and the stars all tell you the time. I grew up near the Choptank, and it changes as you follow it upstream. Notice how it changes for Harriet, and why she walks in the water. Near the end, watch what she decides at a dark house.

Hey, it’s Marcus. Last time, Harriet handed a Quaker woman a note and got a broom back. Today we read two chapters, and they carry her a long way: from house to house on the Underground Railroad, and all the way to Philadelphia. Here’s today’s question, the one I keep circling in my paper: when Harriet finally gets her freedom, what does it feel like, and is anything missing?

Freedom Watch: free, but not yet whole. Harriet has dreamed about crossing the line to freedom for a long time. Watch what she finds when she gets there, and who is around her. When I go back to the Choptank, I always think about the people who never got to leave. So ask yourself: can freedom feel complete while the people you love are still waiting?

Two chapters today, so keep a running list of stops as you go. Watch the clothes Harriet wears from place to place, because each outfit has a job to do. Look for a room that isn’t where you’d expect it. In Chapter 9, notice the moments when her mind goes back home. And listen closely to the man she meets near the end.
